criteria.description: MRI units must have received FDA pre-market approval and operate within approved parameters.
criteria.source_quote: Coverage is limited to MRI units that have received FDA pre-market approval.

criteria.description: Lumbar MRI may be indicated for patients with a red-flag condition.
criteria.source_quote: Lumbar MRI may be indicated for a patient with a “red-flag” condition , such as a suspected tumor, infection, herniated intervertebral disc with nerve compression, or a major neurological problem.

criteria.description: For non-red flag conditions, MRI may be appropriate after one month of symptoms.
criteria.source_quote: For a "non-red flag" condition, the MRI may be appropriate after 1 month of symptoms.

criteria.description: For non-red flag low back pain syndrome, patients must undergo and fail a trial of conservative management lasting at least four weeks.
criteria.source_quote: MRI will be covered only if the patient has not responded to a reasonable trial of conservative management lasting at least four weeks.

criteria.description: The information gained from the test must be expected to be used for medical decision-making and affect treatment choices.
criteria.source_quote: When a lumbar MRI is ordered, Medicare expects that the information gained from the test will be used for medical decision-making.

criteria.description: If duplicating or complementing other imaging studies like a CT scan, documentation must support medical necessity for both studies.
criteria.source_quote: Documentation should support the medical necessity for the need for both studies.

criteria.description: Each payable interpretation must include a complete, separately identifiable written report addressing relevant clinical issues, comparative data, and test findings.
criteria.source_quote: Each payable interpretation must include a complete, written report similar to one that is prepared by a specialist in the field.

exclusions: A lumbar MRI used to evaluate uncomplicated degenerative disc disease or herniated nucleus pulposus when a surgical intervention or other aggressive treatment (e.g. intervertebral joint injection) is not under consideration
When the findings will not affect the treatment choices
Investigational uses including measurement of blood flow, spectroscopy, imaging of cortical bone and calcifications, and procedures involving spatial resolution of bone or calcifications
A lumbar MRI that is an unnecessary duplication of other imaging studies (such as a spinal CT scan)
Patients with an allergy to contrast media
When the technical component is performed without the professional component
Additional payment for multiple MRI’s such as in the reclining and upright positions (multi-position MRI)
